notes: After a few early R&D runs the Runner clicked for credits for eight straight turns, banking 39 credits while the Corp scored from lightly iced remotes. It then ran a second time into a Merlin it had already seen with three cards in grip and was flatlined.

The Corp kept putting agendas behind Crick and Swordsman after the Runner had shown it could walk through them, and later behind a lone Pup, losing three agendas. Its economy and late scoring were sensible, though the Interns play and the Cyberdex purge did nothing.
The Runner installed nothing all game and clicked for credits up to 58 while the Corp scored freely. Its only runs were into unrezzed ice it had no breakers for.

The Corp put a second Project Beale into the same server right after the Runner had passed its lone Turnpike to steal the first, while sitting on about 20 unspent credits. After that it scored GFI behind Resistor and used Closed Accounts well.

Steady R&D pressure won the game, but the Runner aimed Security Testing at Archives and then ran R&D. It also spent down to 1 credit on R&D Interface before a run, so it could not pay Femme Fatale and lost both the breaker and cards to Lancelot.

The Corp piled up 20 or more credits and drew into a full hand it then had to discard, but protected HQ and R&D only with Pop-up Windows. Agendas held in HQ and on top of R&D were stolen, and Psychographics was played for no effect.
The Runner correctly kept hitting HQ through Drafter, which cannot end the run, and won on turn 6. The only oddity was installing Boomerang and never using it.

The Runner sold its own breakers (Cerberus, Self-modifying Code) to Aesop's Pawnshop and then clicked for credits up to 50 without making a single run. The Corp scored agendas it advanced over several turns without any challenge.

The Corp rushed to 6 points early, then spent about nine turns clicking for credits and discarding with 20 or more banked instead of finding and scoring a last agenda. R&D stayed behind a single Pop-up Window, and an early Beale behind another Pop-up Window was stolen.

A turn-1 agenda behind one ice and an open R&D gave up early points, but after that the Corp scored efficiently behind Tollbooth with PAD Campaign economy. Installing and trashing Cyberdex with no virus to purge was wasted.

After two Hostile Takeovers the Corp made no attempt to score for about 20 turns despite 15-30 credits and a deeply iced remote. It spent two whole turns purging a single Yusuf counter and kept advancing ice; it won only because the Runner ran into Mausolus.

Good central runs got the Runner to 6 points, but it sold useful cards to Pawnshop and was hit early by a Snare. It then ran with three cards in grip into an unrezzed ice and fresh remote against a deck already known to play Snare and meat damage, and was flatlined.

The Corp left its HQ ice unrezzed and lost two SSL Endorsements on turns 2-3, after wasting Punitive Counterstrike for 0 damage. It later sat on 30-40 credits bouncing and reinstalling Chiyashi with Blue Sun, never layering ice on R&D or pushing agendas.

The Runner ran an open R&D four times per turn, so every run after the first saw the same top card. It installed no breakers at all and then clicked for credits while the Corp scored three agendas from a single-Wraparound remote.
Solid play: Corroder on R&D, Temüjin on HQ, trashing key assets, and a well-timed final remote run to win. Paying 20 credits to New Angeles City Hall to dodge four tags was costly but defensible.

The Corp never built a scoring remote, clicking for credits and discarding while it held agendas in an HQ that had no ice once Tollbooth was trashed. Four agendas were stolen from HQ, and it played Psychographics for no effect and tried to trash Liberated Account three times.

The Runner reinstalled Chameleon for 2 credits every turn, even on turns it made no run, which kept it stuck at 0-5 credits. It got only occasional R&D runs and had no way to contest the Corp's remote.

The Corp built a four-ice remote by turn 4 and never put an agenda in it, holding Corporate Sales Team and Nisei MK II while clicking up to 44 credits. It discarded every turn, sending a Nisei MK II to Archives where it was stolen, and never added ice to the single-Eli R&D.

The Corp kept feeding assets into a remote guarded only by Turnpike, where the Runner trashed them, including a SanSan it had just paid 6 to rez. Even so, it then scored three agendas cleanly behind Resistor.

The Runner repeated R&D runs that saw the same top card, then from turn 8 mostly clicked for credits up to 37. It let the Corp advance two GFIs in Server 7 over several turns without contest and stole only one Vitruvius.
